report.verdict: A senior payments engineer with strong Go and ledger work, but some leadership and partnership details aren't shown.
write_up: Your resume is strong because it connects payments engineering work to the demands placed on it: payout volume, a zero-downtime ledger migration and faster balance reads. A recruiter can see why your Lumen Ledger work belongs in the conversation for Cobalt Pay.

The balance API line is a great model: it names the change, the before and after, and the approach you used. Your experience also leads your education, and the progression from insurance to freight technology to payments is easy to follow.

For this posting, bring your Kafka work forward and add any relevant collaboration or technical leadership you can substantiate. Your resume is unlikely to be the thing holding you back; the competition for the role and a referral can also matter.

cards.line: Cut p99 latency on the balance API from 900 ms to 140 ms by moving reads to a Kafka-fed cache
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It gives the recruiter a concrete service and a measurable improvement without making them guess what you changed.

cards.line: Led the migration of the ledger from a single Postgres instance to a sharded cluster with zero downtime over six weekends
cards.cannot_tell: For a role above senior engineer, a cross-team architecture decision would show how your leadership reached beyond the migration itself.
cards.example: Led the migration of the ledger from a single Postgres instance to a sharded cluster with zero downtime over six weekends, with [cross-team architecture decision] for [systems affected]
cards.question: Did you make a cross-team architecture decision for this migration, and which systems did it affect?

fit.why: Your headline and current payments platform role both point to senior backend engineering.

fit.note: Your payouts service, ledger migration and Kafka-fed cache are directly relevant to money movement. Bring the event-driven billing line higher in the Harborview role to make that experience easier to spot.
